title: Report Writing and Summarisation — news & event report format
notes: **What it is:** factual, third-person, past-tense reporting of an event (sports day, blood donation camp) — not a story, not an opinion.

**Structure:** Headline (short, factual) → Byline ('By a Staff Reporter') + dateline ('Kathmandu, 12 May:') → Lead paragraph answering WHO did WHAT, WHERE, WHEN, WHY in 2–3 sentences → Body in chronological order → a short quotation from the chief guest → closing outcome.
**Tense/voice grammar:** past simple for every event; passive voice is standard for ceremony facts ('trophies were distributed'); reported speech for quotes; third person only — never 'I'.
**Summarisation partner skill:** compress any passage into its core idea in your own words within the word limit — keep the author's viewpoint, drop examples and repetition.
**Full guide:** Full model answers, starting-line banks and exam tips: [/knowledge/writing](/knowledge/writing).

**Report skeleton (classified)**

| Section | Content | Tense |
|---|---|---|
| Title | What was done | — |
| Introduction | Purpose, scope, background | Past/present |
| Findings | Facts observed, numbered | Past |
| Conclusion | Meaning of findings | Present |
| Recommendation | What to do next | Should/modal |

**Report vs essay**

| Aspect | Report | Essay |
|---|---|---|
| Headings | Yes | Usually no |
| Data | Central | Supportive |
| Voice | Impersonal | Can be personal |
| Purpose | Inform and act | Argue or explore |

examShortTricks: Trick 1: Report skeleton: title, byline, intro (what/when/where), body (details in past tense, third person), conclusion (outcome/recommendation) — the five blocks are the marks.
Trick 2: Reports are OBJECTIVE: no 'I think', no exaggeration; add one quotation or number for credibility.
Trick 3: Summary method: read twice → one line per paragraph → join with connectors → compress to 1/3 length in your own words; never copy sentences.
practiceQuestions: Q. Write a report on a school science exhibition in about 120 words. (4 marks) — title, byline, 5W intro, two body details, closing outcome.
Q. How long should a summary be? (1 mark) — about one-third of the original, in your own words.
